matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the difference between the two sides; this tells you how much the total must increase or decrease.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the equation, before enumerating stick moves.
matchstick.example: Changing sticks without first checking the numeric values, leading to an equation that still doesn't balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Generate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character (including operators) to any other character, respecting stick orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After determining the needed numeric change, before evaluating candidates.
matchstick.example: Skipping moves that involve taking a vertical stick from '+' to create a new numeral, thus missing the correct solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and verify that the net change matches the required discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate evaluation, after listing possible moves.
matchstick.example: Accepting a move that reduces a numeral by 5 when the equation needs a +9 adjustment.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick leaves a '-' (horizontal only), which is a valid operator. Ensure the source '+' remains a valid operator after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from a '+' operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal stick from '+' and leaving only a vertical line, which is not a recognized operator.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously altering both operators; both resulting operators must be valid (e.g., '+' to '-', '-' to '+').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a candidate move involves moving a stick between two operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '+' and ending up with a single‑stick '=', which is invalid, and a malformed '+'.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral can increase (or decrease) its value by the needed amount, move a stick from an operator to that numeral (or to create a new numeral), while keeping the source operator valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a change that can be achieved by augmenting a numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from '+' to a numeral and forming 'XIIII', which is not a standard Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', each side must have at least one valid numeral, and all symbols must be valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, before checking numeric equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '=', leaving the equation without an equality sign.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Map common single‑stick changes (e.g., X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) to their numeric value changes (±5, ±4, ±9) and use these to quickly assess whether a direct numeral transformation can resolve the discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating moves that modify a numeral directly.
matchstick.example: Changing X to V (−5) when the required change is +9, so the move cannot fix the equation.

matchstick.title: Preserve the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The equation must retain exactly one '=', so you cannot relocate a stick from the '=' sign; doing so would either destroy the equality sign or produce an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During enumeration of source characters for stick relocation; exclude the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into '-', and leaving the equation without an '=' sign.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting Roman numerals
matchstick.principle: After any stick move that alters a numeral, verify that the resulting numeral follows standard Roman numeral conventions (no more than three consecutive I's, proper subtractive notation, no non‑standard forms like 'XIIII').
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a stick move to a numeral, before accepting the candidate.
matchstick.example: Creating 'XIIII' (four consecutive I's) which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without checking that the source or destination character remains a recognized Roman numeral or operator, producing shapes that are not valid symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character corresponds to a known valid symbol.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on a plausible visual change but does not compute the resulting integer values to confirm the equation balances.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the integer values of both sides after the move and ensure they are equal.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the process of moving a stick, the model accidentally deletes a character or fails to include it in the final answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final equation contains all original characters (except for the moved stick) and exactly one '=', with at least one numeral on each side.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing '+' to '-' (or vice versa) alters the arithmetic, but the model does not recalculate the effect on the total.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator changes, recompute the arithmetic expression accordingly.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either adds a new stick or removes one without relocating it, violating the exactly‑one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly track that one stick is taken from a source character and placed onto a destination character; no sticks are created or destroyed.
